Nau mai, haere mai

Stronger governance.
Thriving marae.

We’re bringing together trustees and whānau from four Wairarapa marae for two days of shared learning, practical governance skills and planning for the future of our marae.

Building on the insights from each marae’s Governance Aromatawai, we’ll share experiences, strengthen our understanding and explore practical ways to support our marae and the next generation of leaders.

YOU’RE INVITED

Whether you’re a current trustee or whānau member keen to learn and contribute, nau mai, haere mai. No previous governance experience is needed.

What we’ll explore

Three pathways to stronger governance

Practical conversations and activities designed to help each marae move from understanding to action.

01 · TEKOTEKO

Our responsibilities

  • Who does what — and why it matters
  • Mapping trustees, committees and operational roles
  • Clarifying governance and administration responsibilities
02 · TĀHUHU

Strategic priorities

  • Choosing priorities that balance whānau and marae outcomes with practical foundations
  • Comparing project ideas through a decision-making framework
  • Turning priorities into next steps
03 · POU TUARONGO

Succession & continuity

  • Growing capability across our whānau
  • Understanding trustee numbers and the skills we need
  • Strengthening induction and succession pathways
The wānanga programme

Two days of practical progress

Six facilitated sessions will help us understand our governance structures, explore solutions and plan meaningful next steps. The programme may be refined as preparations progress.

Our way of understanding governance

The Whare Tūpuna Governance Framework

Just as each part of the whare has its own purpose and supports the whole, effective marae governance depends on different responsibilities working together.

Our wānanga draws on three dimensions of the Whare Tūpuna Framework: TEKOTEKO (leadership); TĀHUHU (strategy); POU TUARONGO (future-proofing).

Guiding the kōrero

Meet your facilitators

Our Te Whare Hukahuka facilitators bring experience in Māori governance, strategy, community leadership and practical organisational development. Two facilitators will be joining us to guide the kōrero over the two days.

Pou Whakauruuru

Chevourne Taukiri

Programme Delivery Manager & Facilitator

Taranaki Whānui, Ngaati Korokii-Kahukura ki Waikato, Ngāti Toa, Ngāti Maniapoto, Ngāti Koata, Ngāti Rārua

Chevourne brings experience across marae, hapū, whānau and community governance, with a collaborative, values-led approach to facilitation, planning and relationship management.

Read more about Chevourne

Her professional experience spans the public service, vocational education, community and private sectors. She is committed to strengthening governance that upholds tikanga, fosters collaborative leadership and creates pathways for current and future generations.

Pou Tokomanawa

Shay Wright

Executive Director & Lead Facilitator

Te Rarawa, Te Mahurehure (Ngāpuhi), Ngāruahine

Shay co-founded Te Whare Hukahuka in 2013 and has worked with leadership teams across Aotearoa and beyond on governance, strategy and social impact.

Read more about Shay

Raised on whānau land in the Far North, Shay brings experience across Māori leadership, entrepreneurship, organisational strategy and governance. His work focuses on strengthening Indigenous organisations and preparing future leaders.
